source_text: Praesente ac teste me ipso accipite quid evenerit. Parentes forte fugientes, dum trepidi minus consulunt, sub nutricis alimento parvulam filiam reliquerunt; relictam nutrix detulit ad magistratus. Illi ei, apud idolum quo populus confluebat, quod carnem necdum posset edere per aetatem, panem mero mixtum, quod tamen et ipsum de immolatione pereuntium supererat, tradiderunt. Recepit filiam postmodum mater. Sed facinus puella commissum tam loqui et indicare non potuit, quam nec intelligere prius potuit nec arcere. Ignoratione igitur obreptum est ut sacrificantibus nobis eam secum mater inferret. Sed enim puella mixta cum sanctis, precis nostrae et orationis impatiens, nunc ploratu concuti, nunc mentis aestu coepit fluctuabunda jactari, et velut tortore cogente, quibus poterat indiciis conscientiam facti in simplicibus adhuc annis rudis anima fatebatur. Ubi vero solemnibus adimpletis calicem diaconus offerre praesentibus coepit, et accipientibus caeteris locus ejus advenit, faciem suam parvula instinctu divinae majestatis avertere, os labiis obturantibus premere, calicem recusare. Perstitit tamen diaconus, et reluctanti licet de sacramento calicis infudit. Tunc sequitur singultus et vomitus. In corpore atque ore violato Eucharistia permanere non potuit. Sanctificatus in Domini sanguine potus de pollutis visceribus erupit. Tanta est potestas Domini, tanta majestas! Secreta tenebrarum sub ejus luce detecta sunt, sacerdotem Dei nec occulta crimina fefellerunt.
thought_title: A Lapsed Child's Reaction to the Eucharist
pass_a_gloss: With me myself present and witnessing, receive what happened. Perhaps the parents, while fleeing and being less cautious because they were anxious, left their little daughter under the nourishment of a nurse; the nurse left behind brought her to the magistrates. They, at the idol where the people were gathering, because she was not yet able to eat flesh due to her age, handed her bread mixed with wine, which also was a remainder of the immolation of the perishing. The mother received the daughter afterwards. But the girl was not able to speak or indicate the deed that had been committed, as much as she was not able to understand beforehand or prevent. Therefore, it happened through ignorance that, while we were sacrificing, the mother brought her with her. But indeed the girl, mixed with the saints, being unable to endure our prayer and supplication, began to be tossed about, now shaken by weeping, now by a surge of mind, and, as if forced by a torturer, with the signs that she could, the simple soul, still in her early years, confessed the consciousness of the deed. When indeed the solemnities were completed and the deacon began to offer the cup to those present, and the turn came to her, the little girl, inspired by the divine majesty, turned her face away, pressed her mouth shut with her lips, and refused the cup. The deacon, however, persisted, and, although she struggled, poured the sacrament of the cup into her. Then follows hiccuping and vomiting. The Eucharist was not able to remain in the violated body and mouth. The drink sanctified in the Lord's blood burst forth from the polluted innards. So great is the power of the Lord, so great is His majesty! The secrets of darkness were detected under His light, and the hidden crimes did not deceive God's priest.

pass_b_english: I was present and saw it all myself, so take this account as true. The parents, fleeing in panic and hardly thinking straight, left their baby daughter in the care of a nurse; the nurse then brought the child to the magistrates. There, at the idol where the crowds gathered, the officials gave her bread soaked in wine — since she was too young for solid food — wine that had itself been left over from the sacrifices of the dying. Later the mother reclaimed her daughter. But the little girl could neither speak of what had been done to her nor even understand it beforehand, let alone resist it. So, in ignorance, her mother brought her along when we were offering sacrifice. Yet the child, now among the saints, could not endure our prayers and supplications; she began to be tossed about, now shaken by weeping, now by a surge of mind, and as if driven by a torturer she confessed, with the few signs she could manage, the awareness of the deed in her simple soul, still so young. When the solemn rites were finished and the deacon began offering the cup to those present, her turn came. Moved by a divine impulse, the little girl turned her face away, pressed her lips tight, and refused the cup. The deacon persisted, however, and, even as she struggled, poured the sacrament of the cup into her. Then came hiccups and vomiting. The Eucharist could not remain in a violated body and mouth; the drink sanctified by the Lord's blood burst forth from her polluted innards. Such is the power of the Lord, such is his majesty! The secrets of darkness are laid bare under his light, and hidden crimes cannot deceive God's priest.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful literal gloss, and Pass B provides a fluent English rendering that preserves all nuances of agency, modality, and the specific details of the narrative (e.g., the girl's inability to understand or prevent the act, the deacon's persistence despite her reluctance, and the physical reaction).
